meetings.title: Creativity across business
meetings.summary: Five timed rounds, five DECA career areas, one idea you build and defend

agenda.label: Creative thinking is a business skill.
Five rounds. Five ways to be creative.
Build a budget that survives bad news.
Sell the same thing three different ways.
Turn a complaint into something people would choose.
Fix ten bad minutes for a real person.
Kill the lunch line without spending anything.
Which of your five is actually worth building?
Make the concept sketch.
Sixty seconds each. Say the choice, not the idea.

meetings.title: Meet the business
meetings.summary: Take a real business apart, meet the people who run one, and leave with five questions

agenda.label: A business model is a plan for making money.
Take one apart. Then choose your own.
Fill four boxes for a business you already know.
Write the promise, without using the word quality.
Describe one customer so exactly that someone could find them.
Ask the business the things you could not find out.
Pick the business you will study for six weeks.
Write five questions you cannot answer yet.
Read your hardest question out loud. Someone may already know where to look.

meetings.title: Business research lab
meetings.summary: Five rounds of hunting, judging, and throwing sources out

agenda.label: Two kinds of data, and you need both.
Keep this in front of you all meeting.
Throw a source out and be able to say why.
Answer three of your five questions, with receipts.
Name who your business could lose a customer to.
Put your findings in four boxes and find the empty one.
Write three questions you will actually send or ask.
Write up your findings so a stranger could check them.
Name the source you threw out and the finding that surprised you.

meetings.title: Write the business spotlight
meetings.summary: Five writing rounds that assemble into the one-page paper before you leave

agenda.label: A paper is one claim, held up by evidence.
Write three claims. Keep one.
Sort your findings under the claim and find the orphans.
Underline every sentence you cannot back up.
Write four sentences in this exact order.
Write the sentence only you could write.
Your page is done when all eight are filled.
Assemble the page and submit it.
Say your claim out loud in one sentence.

meetings.title: Create for a real audience
meetings.summary: Four decisions, five rounds, one ad the business will actually see

agenda.label: An ad is the promotion decision.
Judge two real ads before you make your own.
Two ads for the same bakery.
Write your audience in one sentence, from your own paper.
Get it to ten words and check it against the truth.
Show a partner your layout for three seconds.
Name exactly what you want them to do next.
Make the ad and write the reasoning.
Send it to the business with one specific question attached.

meetings.title: Build your quiz app
meetings.summary: Write it, build it, and have someone else break it, all in one meeting

agenda.label: Being tested beats re-reading.
Testing wins, but only after a delay.
Write three questions without looking at your paper.
Write one question of each kind.
Make the wrong answers hard to dismiss.
Write feedback that teaches, not feedback that judges.
Hand it to someone and watch it break.
Ship the quiz and fix what the tester found.
You built something other people can use.

meetings.title: Showcase your work
meetings.summary: Assemble it, name what it proves, and say it out loud in sixty seconds

agenda.label: Sixty seconds is a real format.
List everything you made. You have forgotten half of it.
Build the portfolio in this order.
Write three lines in the form skill, artifact, proof.
The same skills, written two ways.
Write the pitch to these four time blocks.
Say it out loud three times before anyone important hears it.
Present, then take real feedback.
You started with curiosity. You are leaving with evidence.
